text: Is the baby feeding well and having regular wet diapers, or has he been lethargic and difficult to rouse? I need to assess if this is physiological jaundice or something more serious like hemolysis or infection.

speaker: Doctor
text: Has there been any blood type incompatibility between the mother and the baby, such as Rh or ABO mismatch? Also, are you noticing any signs of bruising or bleeding from the umbilical cord?

speaker: Doctor
text: Has the baby passed any dark, tarry stools or pale, clay-colored stools, and is his urine a normal light yellow or unusually dark? I need to rule out biliary atresia or other liver issues.

speaker: Patient
text: His stools are a normal yellow color, and his urine is light yellow as expected. There have been no changes in his bowel habits or urination.

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the jaundice started after 24 hours, the baby is feeding well, and there are no signs of hemolysis or liver dysfunction, this appears to be physiological jaundice. Are there any other symptoms you have noticed, such as fever, vomiting, or poor weight gain?

speaker: Patient
text: No, he has no fever, vomiting, or poor weight gain. He seems perfectly healthy otherwise.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the onset after 24 hours, normal feeding, and absence of other symptoms, this presentation is classic for physiological jaundice. DIAGNOSIS READY: Physiological Jaundice
